courses.query: elevation profile and terrain difficulty
courses.details: The NYC Half Marathon features a challenging but achievable course with rolling hills and varied terrain throughout. Early sections include two hills near Prospect Park, a bridge crossing, and four miles on the FDR Drive, followed by a 5K through Times Square and Central Park. The final 5K presents a gradual uphill climb leading to the finish, though the last section through Central Park features relatively easier terrain with minor elevation changes near Bethesda Fountain about 400 meters from the finish. While not the most difficult half marathon, the course presents opportunities for runners to achieve strong performances on a day when conditions align well.

courses.details: This is an educational explanation of elevation and terrain concepts rather than a specific race course. Elevation refers to height above sea level measured in feet or meters, which affects climate, vegetation, and weather conditions. A terrain profile is a cross-sectional diagram showing elevation changes along a route, with vertical exaggeration to display slope variations, peaks, and valleys. These concepts are commonly used for hiking and outdoor planning to assess route difficulty, as well as for engineering, geological analysis, and geographic research.

courses.query: Philadelphia Marathon course elevation profile terrain race day conditions
courses.details: The Philadelphia Marathon is mostly flat with a maximum elevation of 136 feet, though it features rolling hills through Fairmount Park (miles 7-15) that make it approximately 1.6% slower than a completely flat course. The route begins flat through historic downtown Philadelphia past Independence Hall and City Hall, then ascends through Fairmount Park with the most challenging terrain at miles 7, 9, and 12, before descending to scenic Kelly Drive along the Schuylkill River. The course highlights an energetic out-and-back on Manayunk's Main Street (miles 19-21) with fantastic crowd support, and finishes at the Philadelphia Museum of Art with a gentle final incline. Expect cold, dry weather around 43°F with light winds under 10 mph, and arrive by 6 a.m. for the 6:50 a.m. corral entry at the Benjamin Franklin Parkway start line.
